summary: Assess fraud schemes, evaluate controls and build monitoring plans through practical exercises. Explore the five-day intermediate course.
lede: Fraud prevention training helps audit, compliance and control practitioners identify fraud schemes and assess exposure. It covers rating likelihood and significance, mapping preventive and detective controls, and prioritizing residual risks. Practical exercises address fraud-focused data analytics, allegation follow-up and monitoring, using work products such as a risk register, heat map and response plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for practitioners who assess fraud exposures, examine controls, support investigations or coordinate mitigation and monitoring. It suits intermediate-level professionals who need to connect process knowledge, evidence and follow-up actions in a usable fraud risk assessment.
modules: Fraud Scheme Inventory and Assessment Matrix
Likelihood, Significance and Risk Heat Maps
prerequisites: This intermediate course suits you if you have working familiarity with fraud risk, internal audit, compliance or internal controls. No coding or programming is required; exercises use fraud assessment artefacts and spreadsheet-based templates.
